categories.label: Negative parallelism
categories.why: The single most reliable tell. Models reach for it to sound profound without adding information.
categories.fix: Keep at most one, and only where the contrast carries the argument. State the claim directly instead.

categories.label: Rule of three
categories.why: Three parallel items in a row. Classical rhetoric, but repeated it produces a mechanical cadence.
categories.fix: Use two items, or four of unequal length and shape.

categories.label: Signposting
categories.why: Talking about the text instead of saying the thing.
categories.fix: Delete the phrase. The sentence after it is the actual sentence.

categories.label: Inflated vocabulary
categories.why: Words models overproduce to signal importance.
categories.fix: Replace with the plainest word that carries the meaning.

categories.label: Trailing participles
categories.why: A clause bolted onto the end to imply causation that was never argued.
categories.fix: Cut it, or make it its own sentence with a real subject.

categories.label: Vague attribution
categories.why: Authority with no source behind it.
categories.fix: Name the source, or drop the claim.

categories.label: Formulaic opening
categories.why: The stock first line of generated text.
categories.fix: Open on something concrete: a scene, a number, a claim someone would argue with.

categories.label: Formulaic closing
categories.why: The tidy bow. Models cannot resist restating the thesis with symmetry.
categories.fix: End on the part you have not resolved, or on a question you actually want answered.
